text:
Situation: Rocuronium bromide has been on the FDA drug shortage list since 2023-02-15 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 7.1 days of the 5 mL presentation, Corvale General 19.2 days, and Corvale Lakeside 28.5 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2023-02-15. The Hikma Farmaceutica (Portugal) plant that makes the Hikma-labeled vials used at Corvale East, Corvale General, and Corvale Lakeside was inspected on 2023-02-03 and classified VAI, 12 days before the posting. The same plant received a VAI classification after an inspection ending 2023-04-21, 65 days after the posting. An earlier inspection ending 2020-03-06 was classified VAI, 1,076 days before the posting. The Hospira, Inc. plant supplying the alternate manufacturer option was last inspected with an NAI classification on 2025-02-07.

Our position: Corvale East is critically low on the 5 mL presentation. Corvale Lakeside and Corvale General have sufficient stock to support a transfer while maintaining at least two weeks of supply. The Hospira alternate manufacturer option is approved for use. B. Braun and BE Pharmaceuticals products are not on the FDA shortage list but their labels do not identify a manufacturing plant we can verify.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 13 vials of rocuronium bromide 10 mg/mL, 5 mL from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. If additional supply is needed, transfer 40 vials of rocuronium bromide 10 mg/mL, 5 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
3. Use Hospira, Inc. rocuronium bromide 10 mg/mL as the alternate manufacturer — pharmacist verification required; approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2026-08-13.
4. Evaluate purchase from B. Braun Medical Inc. — buyer to assess; not on FDA shortage list; label names no verifiable plant.
5. Evaluate purchase from BE Pharmaceuticals Inc. — buyer to assess; not on FDA shortage list; label names no verifiable plant.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing or protocol changes; those are for the treating clinicians and the committee.
